claims.claim: On Friday, President Donald Trump signed an executive order waiving newly passed Russia sanctions and said the move was in the US national interest.
claims.episode_span: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order waiving newly passed Russia sanctions
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: United States President Donald Trump has signed an executive order waiving newly-passed Russia sanctions, claiming the move is in the US’s “national interest”.

claims.claim: The Friday order called off planned Russia sanctions days before they were due, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for buying Russian oil and gas.
claims.episode_span: It called off numerous planned Russia-related sanctions, including duties on Russian goods
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: In his executive order on Friday, Trump called off numerous planned Russia-related sanctions days before they were due to take effect, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for buying the country’s oil and gas.

claims.claim: The blocked measures were in legislation Congress passed last month with bipartisan support, named after the late Senator Lindsay Graham, and would have included tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from the five top importers of Russian crude oil or gas, including China and India.
claims.episode_span: tariffs of up to 100 percent on all goods brought into the United States from the five top importers
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: They would have included up to 100 percent tariffs on all goods brought into the US from the five top importers of Russian crude oil or gas, including China and India.

claims.claim: The law could also have penalised countries that knowingly bought Russian oil or gas 30 days after implementation, or that were among the top five helping Moscow circumvent oil sanctions.
claims.episode_span: equal penalties on countries deemed to have knowingly bought oil or gas from Russia 30 days after the law's implementation
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: They could also have imposed equal penalties on countries deemed to have knowingly bought oil or gas from Russia 30 days after the law’s implementation, or to be among the top five countries helping Moscow circumvent sanctions on sales of its oil.

claims.claim: The waiver holds until the Trump administration believes further action is appropriate.
claims.episode_span: The waiver holds until the Trump administration believes further action is appropriate
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: The waiver will hold until the Trump administration believes “further action is appropriate”, according to the executive order.

claims.claim: Earlier this month Trump announced a deal to bring Russian diesel into global markets, and the US Treasury waived sanctions on Russian diesel sales until April 2027.
claims.episode_span: The US Treasury waived sanctions on Russian diesel sales until April 2027.
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: Earlier this month, Trump also announced a deal to bring stocks of Russian diesel into global markets, in a bid to drive down energy prices that have spiked during the US-Israel war on Iran. The US Treasury waived sanctions on Russian diesel sales until April 2027.

claims.claim: Trump said the diesel deal would bring 300,000 tonnes immediately, 500,000 tonnes in November, and 1 million tonnes afterwards.
claims.episode_span: 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel into US and global markets immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November, and 1 million tonnes afterwards
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: According to Trump, that deal would bring 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel into US and global markets “immediately”, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November, and 1 million tonnes afterwards.

claims.claim: President Volodmyr Zelenskyy called the diesel deal a gift to Vladimir Putin that will help fund the war.
claims.episode_span: Zelenskyy slammed the diesel deal as a gift to Russia's President Vladimir Putin
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: Ukraine’s President Volodmyr Zelenskyy slammed Trump’s diesel deal as “a gift” to Russia’s President Vladimir Putin that will help fund his war effort.

claims.claim: Congressman Don Beyer called the sanctions waiver a surrender to Putin that betrays Ukrainian partners and defies congressional intent.
claims.episode_span: the sanctions waiver amounts to a surrender to Putin that betrays Ukrainian partners
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: US Congressman Don Beyer, a Democrat from Virginia, said the sanctions waiver amounts to a “surrender to Putin” that “betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent”.

claims.claim: Vasily Astrov estimated that about 60 cents of every extra dollar in the price of a barrel of Russian oil would end up in Russian state coffers.
claims.episode_span: about 60 cents of every extra dollar in the price of a barrel of Russian oil would end up in state coffers

claims.claim: Kirill Dmitriev hailed the US decision to waive the sanctions as an important and truly historic moment.

claims.supporting_quote: Russian official Kirill Dmitriev, an envoy for Putin, hailed the US decision to waive the sanctions as “an important and truly historic moment”.

claims.claim: CREA said China and India bought 6 billion euros and 3.6 billion euros of Russian crude respectively in September.
claims.episode_span: purchasing 6 billion euros, or 6.74 billion dollars, and 3.6 billion euros, or 4.04 billion dollars, respectively
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: China and India are the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, purchasing 6 billion euros ($6.74bn) and 3.6 billion euros ($4.04bn) worth respectively in September, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a nonprofit think tank.

claims.claim: Valdis Dombrovskis said the diesel volumes are not of macroeconomic significance and doubted Russia could supply them to US quality standards.
claims.episode_span: the volumes are not of any macroeconomic significance
claims.source_title: Trump eases Russia oil sanctions, but is Europe still buying Moscow’s gas?
claims.supporting_quote: “If we look at the volumes, they are not of any macroeconomic significance, and frankly, there are strong doubts whether Russia is even able to supply those volumes, and according also to US quality standards, those are big question marks,” Dombrovskis told the AFP news agency.
